message_spans.text:
Add a `type="pills"` variant to `st.tabs` to show tabs as pills

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `type` parameter to `st.tabs` with a `"pills"` variant that renders the tab headers as pills (rounded, button-like segments) instead of the default underlined tab bar. Keep the same tab behavior — only the visual style of the tab headers changes.

### Why?

The underlined tab style is great for section navigation, but pill-style tabs are a very common, more compact and prominent look — especially for filters, view switchers, and dashboards. Today users approximate this with `st.pills`/`st.segmented_control` plus manual conditional rendering, which is more boilerplate and doesn't give the clean container-per-tab

model that `st.tabs` provides.

### How?

Add a `type` parameter (default preserves today's look):

```python
tab1, tab2, tab3 = st.tabs(["Overview", "Details", "Settings"], type="pills")
with tab1:
    st.write("...")
```

- `type="default"` (or `"underline"`) — current tab bar.
- `type="pills"` — render the tab headers as pills.
- Everything else (content containers, active-tab state, etc.) stays identical.

### Additional Context

- Visually aligns `st.tabs` with the existing pill styling used by `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control`, but with the `st.tabs` container model.
- Design references for the pills style:
  - [Tailwind Plus — Tabs (pill variant)](https://tailwindcss.com/plus/ui-blocks/application-ui/navigation/tabs#component-2a66fc822e8ad55f59321825e5af0980)
  - [Tremor — Tabs, solid variant](https://tremor.so/docs/ui/tabs#example-tabs-solid-variant)

### Checklist

### Summary

Currently, the cache decorators are just simple decorators of a hashable saving with the possibility of clearing the cache.

However, a key component in caching is when the cache was saved.

Currently the only method to now this is by caching the result with a timestamp, which is unpractical.

So I'm thinking about a ´´´cached_function.time()´´´ method for knowing when it was last cached.

### Why?

Because knowing the time of the cache would be very comprehensive for:
- Not clearing cache everytime an update is needed, checking first if the time of the cache is soon enough
- Simply adding a display of Last Updated at

### How?
